consumer.name: llama-server
consumer.evidence: ELF dynamic import inventory and pinned source inspection only; no runtime call trace or GPU execution

presentation.anchor: Expose one selected CUDA 7.0 device. Device properties and memory queries report that physical anchor's native values; no pair capacity or SM count is synthesized.
presentation.pair: Expose one logical CUDA device backed by one compute anchor. Direct VMM allocation gateways may use the configured peer-backed canonical VA. Generic native kernels are forwarded only to the registered anchor and retain all managed allocations through a completion prefix; no kernel splitting or peer compute claim is made.

interception.driver_resolver: cuGetProcAddress_v2 returns frontdoor function pointers for qualified wrapped entries while preserving driver version and legacy/PTDS selection. Unknown Driver entries fail closed in pair mode.
interception.runtime_resolver: cudaGetDriverEntryPoint and cudaGetDriverEntryPointByVersion apply the same wrapper mapping to successfully resolved qualified Driver entries.
interception.native_lookup: Wrappers try RTLD_NEXT, then resolve from the exact already-loaded libcudart/libcuda ELF object via its load path and RTLD_NOLOAD. Resolved native handles remain pinned for process lifetime.
interception.atomic_async: Forwarded async transfers, opaque kernel launches, stream waits and event records run through v200_execution_forward_native. Pair-mode forwards hold a memory submission lease until the resulting stream prefix is retained.

graph_capture.opt_in: --cuda-graphs sets GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=0 for matched controls and V200_GRAPH_CAPTURE=1 only for the pair facade.
graph_capture.pair_execution: During capture, native anchor launches are recorded without inserting ledger events or invoking the non-capture-safe pair operator. After EndCapture, exact eligible Q4_K MMVQ kernel nodes may be rewritten to peer-context functions. Graph replay is tracked as one asynchronous submission.
graph_capture.telemetry: The pair frontdoor ledger records capture, instantiate, update, and a bounded sample of graph replays with matched/re-written node counts.
graph_capture.status: Implementation candidate pending controller-backed graph qualification.

semantic_limits: Graph support is explicit opt-in and limited to the pinned llama runtime capture/instantiate/update/replay path; only exact qualified Q4_K MMVQ graph nodes are peer-rewritten. Other captured operations remain anchor-side.

Launch-time operator numeric verification is skipped during capture because it synchronizes and copies results; graph correctness must be established by the consumer oracle and controller-backed graph qualification.
Applications must keep graph-referenced device allocations alive under CUDA graph lifetime rules; frontdoor completion tracking covers each graph replay, not the entire graph-exec lifetime.
No split arbitrary kernel, cross-owner global/atomic coordination, module-global routing, or NCCL collective is claimed.
The profile is a static import inventory; runtime call frequency and selected llama execution paths remain unproven until controller-backed evidence is recorded.
